blocks.text: A monument with a colonnade and flags in Guayaquil, Ecuador
A pale colonnade with sculptures and national flags in Guayaquil, Ecuador

Early in the morning, transfer by bus to the Itabaca Channel, where your yacht will be waiting.

The crossing to Bartolomé takes about 2 hours. Breakfast is served on board, and you’ll spend part of the crossing at dawn. Dolphins and other marine animals sometimes appear alongside the yacht in the morning.

After landing on Bartolomé, start a climb of about 30 minutes. The trail crosses an almost lunar volcanic landscape to the island’s highest point. From the top you can see Santiago, North Seymour, Baltra, Santa Cruz, Rábida, the islet of Sombrero Chino and the famous Pinnacle Rock, a remnant of an ancient volcanic formation. This is one of the Galápagos’ most recognisable views, with dark volcanic slopes rising above pale sand and clear water.

After the descent, continue to the beaches. From the boat, you may spot small Galápagos penguins, which stand about 50 cm tall. They rest by the rocks and swim quickly through the clear water.

Take a short walk through the dunes to the north beach, where pelicans nest. You may see small reef sharks in the water.

At the south beach, there’s time for swimming and snorkelling. Galápagos penguins, sharks, starfish, rays, sea turtles, colourful fish, marine iguanas, sea lions and pelicans can all be found here.

Lunch is served on board after swimming and snorkelling. On the way back, you’ll have another chance to watch the sea and take in the shores of neighbouring islands. Return to Puerto Ayora by evening. In your free time, you can walk along the waterfront and pier or explore the smaller streets of the port town.

**Accommodation:** Villa Laguna 4*.  
**Meals:** breakfast, lunch.
